messages:
maria (infra): Q2 capacity planning kick-off — we need a decision on how many GPUs to buy vs how much short-term rental to keep for the hosted API. cc @ops @finance
jasper: throwing initial numbers: baseline steady-state demand +30% seasonal peak in June/July. baseline 1.2M tokens/min avg -> peak 1.6M tokens/min.
lee: can you paste the throughput->GPU-hour calc?
jasper: sure. quick calc (very rough):
```
- target p95 latency SLO: 250ms
- sample perf: A100-80GB supports ~1.1M tokens/hr under our batching profile
- peak need: 1.6M tokens/min -> 96M tokens/hr
=> ~87 GPU-hours required at peak (96M / 1.1M)
```
so ~90 GPUs concurrently at peak.
anika: APAC routing constraint: we can’t rely on bursting from eu-west due to egress latencies and customer SLAs. need region-local warm pool.
sre-bot: Alert trend: 14% increase in KV cache eviction rate in the hosted-api prod cluster over last 14 days. Correlates with higher token sizes from a few large customers.
lee: eviction increase means more early context recompute -> per-token cost up ~6%. factoring that in bumps effective GPU requirement to ~95 at peak.
jasper: cost notes: on-demand rental is ~ $5.2 / GPU-hour for our provider region, 1-year reserved purchase equivalent TCO (amortized) ~ $2.1 / GPU-hour assuming 3yr life and infra costs.
sam (finance): those are in the ballpark. we have a Q2 incremental capex target of $1.2M available if leadership approves buys.
maria (infra): tradeoffs: buys give ~2x lower unit cost but reduce flexibility; rentals cover peaks and uncertain demand. lean toward a blended approach.
anika: can we narrow to a concrete proposal? e.g., buy N for baseline, rent M for 20-30% surge, maintain warm pool of K GPUs in APAC.
jasper: proposal: buy 50 GPUs (covers steady-state + small cushion), rental pool 40 GPUs for seasonal peaks, APAC warm pool 8 GPUs reserved in region, and reserve 6 GPUs as preemptible for batch jobs that can be evicted.
lee: ops implications: buying 50 + renting 40 means warm-up / model cache priming matters. we should schedule rolling priming jobs and keep prefix caches persisted. warms would add ~2 hours of prep per device after boot.
sre-bot: Note: last auto-scaling incident (2026-01-17) was due to slow node initialization causing transient 10% p95 latency spikes during scale events. recommend parallel priming.
maria (infra): action item: if we buy 50, capex ~ $1.05M (hardware+networking+racks), ops cost for provisioning ~ $45k. rentals at 40 for 3 months peak -> estimated ~$0.6M. totals fit the capex+opex envelope.
sam (finance): confirm numbers. rental estimate assumes average 60% utilization during peak months. if utilization lower, rental spend drops proportionally.
anika: region constraint: APAC procurement lead time for racks is +6 weeks. if we plan buys, order by end of April to land before June. otherwise rentals are our only option for APAC bursts.
lee: one more risk: firmware compatibility on a minority batch of SKUs from supplier X. ops recommends a 10-unit smoke test before full provisioning.
jasper: alternative smaller-buy scenario: buy 30 GPUs, rent 60 during peaks. upsides: lower capex, more flexibility. downsides: higher expected opex (~ +$400k).
maria (infra): preference leaning purchase-heavy but still blended. propose we present two options to exec: (A) buy 50 + rent 40 (capex heavy, lower unit cost), (B) buy 30 + rent 60 (capex light, higher opex). include APAC warm pool & priming SOPs.
sam (finance): I'll run the NPV on both and return numbers by EOD tomorrow.
anika: ops ask: add a requirement that rented nodes must support our KV cache persistence patch or we will not put model-primed traffic on them.
lee: agree. also sched docs for priming scripts: add `--parallelism 12` to reduce wall time. snippet: 
```
./prime_nodes.sh --model redwood-7b --nodes 12 --parallelism 12
```
maria (infra): OK next steps: sam runs financials, ops validates rental SKUs + priming test, procurement drafts PO timeline. meet Thurs 10am to decide. :calendar:
jasper: noted. I'll update the capacity model spreadsheet and add a sensitivity tab for +/-10/20/30% demand variance.
lee: I'll schedule the smoke test once procurement has sample SKUs.
nana (random): :wave: (noted the meeting)
maria (infra): thanks all — thread pinned to capacity planning channel for visibility. :thumbsup:
